text:
morgan: heads up — running into a weird leak in the sampleapp that wraps generator streaming. curious if others have seen this pattern.

morgan: repro steps: call generator.Stream(ctx) -> we wrap it with a small shim that does auth refresh op in background and forwards tokens. if ctx is canceled mid-stream, the client returns but the server connection seems to hang for ~30s until auth refresh finishes.

morgan: code sketch:```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(parent)
stream := client.Generator.Stream(ctx, req)
go func(){
  for token := range tokenCh {
    stream.SetAuth(token) // our shim calls into stream internals
  }
}()
// cancel after first chunk -> caller returns, but background goroutine keeps stream alive
cancel()
```

alex: yep i've seen similar when the SDK doesn't treat SetAuth as cancelable. if SetAuth blocks on RPC it can keep the underlying transport alive.

taylor: is this specifically with the generator handshake or with mid-stream auth rotate?

morgan: auth rotate mid-stream. the shim calls into the generator object which acquires a mutex while handshaking. canceling ctx doesn't interrupt that mutex path.

sophie: two angles: 1) make SetAuth nonblocking (swap pointer to token and let send goroutine pick it up), or 2) expose a CancelStream() on the stream client that force-closes connection even if an internal op is mid-flight.

leanne: +1 to nonblocking token swap. ergonomically, people expect context cancel to be a hard stop. adding CancelStream is fine but will be surprising to users unless in docs.

morgan: i'm prototyping both. nonblocking swap is nicer but tricky with existing handshake code that expects synchronous response for auth error.

alex: another option: return an error channel from Stream that closes immediately on ctx cancel, and also provide a Done() method on the returned iter so callers can select on it. that keeps cancellation visible without surfacing raw transport details.

taylor: that maps to patterns we've used in other SDKs. e.g., stream, errCh := client.Gen.StreamWithErr(ctx, req) then select { case <-ctx.Done(): // stop reading case err := <-errCh: // final }

morgan: good idea. sampleapp change would be minimal. i'll try wiring a Done() and errCh.

sophie: also add a short example in onboarding: "if you need to interrupt mid-generation, cancel ctx AND wait on stream.Done() to ensure resources cleaned up." saves a lot of support noise.

devrel-bot: quick note — if you open a draft PR with "stream-done-errch" tag we'll auto-assign reviewers from devex and eng-runtime.

leanne: one gotcha: ensure we don't change streaming API surface in a semver-incompatible way for the GA SDK. maybe add StreamWithCancel or StreamV2 behind feature flag.

morgan: agreed. i'll branch StreamV2 that returns (StreamHandle) with Done() and ForceClose(). will iterate on naming.

alex: when you have a patch, can you add a small sampleapp in /examples/stream-cancel that reproduces the race? it's super helpful for runtime folks.

morgan: yep gonna add that. will ping runtime for kernel hang debugging if ForceClose still hangs.

taylor: thanks — this pattern explains several support tickets where customers saw "generator hung after ctrl-c".

sophie: tl;dr: make auth update nonblocking OR expose explicit force-close + document Done() behavior. both needed for good ergonomics.

morgan: thanks all — i'll open PR and post link here when ready.
